newsitem.title: USA: Mich. Gov signs Detroit casino regulatory bills.
newsitem.headline: Mich. Gov signs Detroit casino regulatory bills.

text.p: Michigan Gov. John Engler has signed Detroit casino regulatory bills that set state and local fees for future licensees and provide for their oversight.
Michigan voters in November approved a referendum allowing up to three land-based casinos in Detroit and setting a preference for two local groups instrumental in placing the question on the ballot.
The laws enacted Thursday require each licensee to pay $8.33 million annual service fees tied to the increase in the consumer price index.
"These bills provide the protection needed to ensure that casinos operating under Proposal E in Detroit function in an ethical, upright manner," Engler said in a statement.
The referendum set the state gaming tax at 18 percent of adjusted gross receipts, with 55 percent of the proceeds for Detroit and 45 percent devoted to fund elementary and secondary education.
Licensees also must pay an annual municipal service fee of $4 million or 1.25 percent of adjusted gross receipts, whichever is greater.

The new laws require unions to register with the Michigan Gaming Control Board and identify casino-related employees. The makeup of the regulatory board will also be monitored and its powers have been expanded.
Political contributions from individuals holding a 1 percent interest in casinos, or their immediate family members, have been banned.
Preliminary casino applications are due August 1.
The Atwater Group and Greektown Casino LLC were the preferred parties included in the referendum. Circus Circus Enterprises Inc has joined with Atwater.
Other interested parties include Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc, MGM Grand Inc, and Detroit businessman Dan Barden, owner and operator of the Majestic Star Casino in Gary, Ind.
Harrah's Entertainment Inc and Mirage Resorts Inc have opted not to seek licenses.
